planting.note: Plant corms in autumn in winter-rainfall climates, or in early spring elsewhere, so growth begins with the cool wet season.

directions: This monotypic Cape corm produces wiry, branching stems carrying airy, open sprays of small nodding flowers, typically cream to pale yellow with fine purple-brown veining. It grows actively through the cool, moist winter and spring months, then dies back to a dormant corm as summer heat and dryness arrive. Plant corms in very well-drained, gritty soil and avoid summer irrigation once foliage has withered. Its delicate, fishing-rod-like flower stems are prized in mixed fynbos bulb plantings and rockeries, where the fine texture contrasts well with denser shrubby companions.

planting.note: Set out nursery plants in spring once frost danger has passed, giving roots a full season to establish before winter.

directions: This fast-growing evergreen shrub bears narrow lance-shaped leaves and produces abundant small tubular flowers, cream to pale yellow and sweetly scented with a honey-like fragrance that draws bees and other pollinators. It tolerates both coastal wind and inland heat once established, and accepts occasional moisture but dislikes waterlogged soil. Light pruning after the main bloom flush keeps growth dense and encourages repeat flowering. It is commonly used in South African indigenous gardens as an informal hedge or screen near water features where its fragrance can be appreciated.
